The Crisis of Evidence
The foundational method of historical science-rigorous
source criticism-has been entirely bypassed. Modern
science continues to uncritically rely on the highly
compromised, biased testimonies of invaders, inquisitors,
and missionaries.

The Objective
Spanish desire for territorial conquest, wealth,
and slave labor in the New World.
The Legal Barrier (Medieval Law)
Indigenous peoples were classified as subjects of
the Crown. It was strictly illegal to enslave,
murder, or rob them without just cause.
The Loophole (Fray Francisco de Vitoria)
Subjects could only be stripped of their rights and
subjected to military force if they committed
heinous crimes against nature-specifically
idolatry, cannibalism, or human sacrifice.
The Myth as Strategy
Accusing the Aztecs of mass human sacrifice
was not a misunderstanding; it was a required
legal fiction to justify genocide, theft, and the
destruction of an advanced civilization.

names, and methods of human sacrifice.

EXHIBIT C: The Missing Physical Evidence
Archaeological synthesis: Excavations by Eduardo Matos Moctezuma at the Templo Mayor have
yielded incredibly few skeletons-completely inconsistent with accounts of mass slaughter.
Furthermore, a skeleton does not equal a murder victim (e.g., European churches are full of bones).
The Tzompantli: Reclassified not as a trophy
rack of murder victims, but as a sacred
reliquary for the honored dead.
